notes: Find a Tender notices are reachable through search snippets only. WebFetch returned 403 on find-tender and 418 on international-pharma. I found no 2025-26 NHS England GMS or Genomics England tender that is a pure sequencing-platform or consumables buy. The relevant awards are outsourced WGS service contracts, so any Illumina content is hidden inside them. The Revvity award gives a derivable all-in £/sample figure but names no sequencer in the snippets. Nothing found shows a non-Illumina platform winning, and nothing shows Illumina-only eligibility. The evidence is thin and mostly neutral. Per-genome price pressure on Illumina is not directly visible. I did not retrieve the full notice text or the tender documents.
how_to_mine: Open https://www.find-tender.service.gov.uk/Notice/008121-2025/PDF (Revvity award, GEL-HE-596-23) and the 2023 contract notice at /Notice/036294-2023/PDF. If the site returns 403, use the OCDS API at https://www.find-tender.service.gov.uk/api/1.0/ocdsRecordPackages/ocds-h6vhtk-04e9ef, or the tendertracker.co.uk and d3tenders.com mirrors. Read the technical specification for any named platform (NovaSeq, 'Illumina or equivalent') and for the per-sample price, plus the lot structure. Also pull the Babies in Focus long-read notices (060131-2025 and 075853-2025, ref GEL-RE-25161), the December 2024 Oxford Nanopore PromethION flow-cell award, and the 047414-2025 notice. Search Contracts Finder for NHS England Genomic Medicine Service lab-hub NGS reagent awards (the GSTT notice of 1 Sep 2026 covers MiSeq reagents, award value unseen). Check the Revvity Q1-Q2 2025 filings for what sequencer its UK lab runs.

items.label: 1B
items.claim: Genomics England's biggest 2025 WGS award went to a services vendor (Revvity) after the open tender failed, at an all-in price of roughly £650 per sample.
items.detail: Award notice dated 6 Mar 2025, ref GEL-HE-596-23, covers extraction, WGS and storage of 44,500 Generation Study newborn samples at £29.2M ex-VAT, about £656 per sample all-in (derived). This is below the 2023 estimate of £40.5M (about £910 per sample), a 28% lower value. The open procedure produced no suitable bidder, so the award was negotiated with a single supplier. The sequencer is not named in the snippets. The lower-than-estimated value is consistent with buyer pricing leverage, but it includes extraction and storage and cannot be turned into a clean Illumina $/Gb figure.
items.source_name: Find a Tender (Genomics England award notice)
items.why_new: Genomics England's 2025 WGS award value and the 28% drop vs the 2023 estimate are not in the known list.

items.label: 1B
items.claim: Genomics England buys long-read WGS as per-sample services from non-Illumina-centric vendors, at roughly £1.3-2.2K per sample.
items.detail: Babies in Focus (tender published 8 Aug 2025) awarded Lot 2 to Eurofins Genomics UK at £1.288M ex-VAT (26 Sep 2025). Lot 1 went to Cambridge University Technical Services at £2.206M ex-VAT (20 Nov 2025). Lot 1 covers 1,000 samples, sequenced 5 Jan-31 Mar 2026, so about £2.2K per sample. The lot 2 sample count was not seen. The buyer had estimated Lot 1 at £1.4M. Newborn WGS spend is being routed to long-read services, which may take some volume away from Illumina short-read. The scale is small, about £3.5M.
items.source_name: Find a Tender (Genomics England, Babies in Focus)
items.why_new: Genomics England's 2025 long-read award values and winners are not in the known list; NHS rare-disease WGS volume is, but not tenders.
